author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating: the partial-load question is genuinely architectural and wants explicit human direction. Engineering basis recap:

Arguments for option (a) — stay fail-fast, just document it explicitly:
- rustls-webpki and most Rust trust-store loaders do fail-fast.
- The crate's '# Contract guarantees' section (PKIX-tit4.13–18 doc pass) already documents fail-fast behavior for from_der_iter.
- Pre-1.0 design closure on the simplest shape; adding partial-load later under non_exhaustive Error is non-breaking.

Arguments for option (b)/(c) — add a partial-load variant:
- The bead lists three real production scenarios (distro bundles with one corrupt cert, in-flight CA rotation, CT-log ingestion). All three are foreseeable for a Tier-1 loader.
- PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 cache-friendliness argues for being able to surface ALL errors at once for replay; fail-fast loses N-1 errors per cache hit.
- AGENTS.md prelaunch framing says 'design for the eventual complete shape': if partial-load is going to land eventually, ship it now while the breaking-change cost is zero.
- Adapter crates (pkix-truststore-system, pkix-truststore-pkcs11) hit this most acutely — one bad slot in an OS keychain or HSM crashes load.

Recommendation if no human pushback within 24h: stay at option (a) (fail-fast, documented). The fail-fast contract is already documented and AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 frames out-of-process retry as the model for transient failures; in-process partial-load adds complexity for a use case that adapter crates can solve at their layer (drop failing iterator items before passing to from_der_iter). The recent partial-load story IS the AiaFetcher contract in pkix-aia (batch_fetch returns Vec<Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>>) — so partial-load lives at the fetcher layer, not the parser layer. That precedent argues for keeping pkix-truststore fail-fast and pushing partial-load discipline to adapters.
